map.Lessons 5-6, 5-7 & 5-8 — nets, surface a: Lessons 5-6, 5-7 & 5-8: nets, surface area of prisms, and surface area of pyramids. The finale of the Brightside build.
map.Previously: the slab cured at 12 cubic m: Last time: the slab cured at exactly 12 cubic metres. Today the lot gets painted, wrapped, and FINISHED.
map.Previously, in Episode 2: the pour went: Last time, in Episode 2: the pour went perfectly and Fenwick's doubled bill was turned away. One week to opening day.
map.Paint for the chests, canvas for the kio: Paint for the chests, canvas for the kiosk roof, and weather sealer for the planters. Everything gets covered.
map.Surface area protocol: unfold the solid: Surface area rule: unfold the solid into its net, a flat map of every face. Then no face can hide from you.
map.Noah chalks candidate box patterns on th: Noah chalks box patterns on the fresh slab. Only one folds shut.
Speed tip: count the squares FIRST. A cube has six faces. A net with five is an instant fail.
map.Counting is necessary, not sufficient. S: Counting is needed, but it is not enough. Six squares can still overlap when folded. Fold it in your head. Every face needs its own landing spot.
map.Reader — pick the net that actually fold: Reader, pick the net that really folds into our storage cube!
map.Which chalk pattern folds into the stora: Which chalk pattern folds into the storage cube? Tap a net. Then tell VEX how many faces every cube net must have.
map.Conceptual: a cube has 6 faces, so its n: Conceptual: a cube has 6 faces, so its net needs exactly 6 squares. AND they must fold so every face lands in its own spot.
map.Procedural: count squares first (elimina: Procedural: count squares first (this removes two). For the rest, fold in your head: in a 2×3 block, squares stack on each other.
map.The supply chest: 6 long, 3 deep, 2 tall: The supply chest: 6 long, 3 deep, 2 tall. Six faces, but only three DIFFERENT ones. Each has a twin on the opposite side.
map.Prism protocol: top & bottom (6×3), fron: Prism rule: top & bottom (6×3), front & back (6×2), two ends (3×2). Three products, each counted TWICE.
map.SA of a rectangular prism = 2(lw + lh +: SA of a rectangular prism = 2(lw + lh + wh). The 2 is not extra. Every face has a twin.
map.The supply chest is a prism, 6 m × 3 m ×: The supply chest is a prism, 6 m × 3 m × 2 m. Find its total surface area. Then we see if one 80 m² can of paint covers it.
map.Conceptual: three DIFFERENT faces — top: Conceptual: three DIFFERENT faces: top (6×3), front (6×2), end (3×2). Each one has an identical twin on the opposite side.
map.Pyramid net: one square + four identical: Pyramid net: one square + four identical triangles. Canvas covers ALL of it. The kiosk has a floor, and floors are faces.
map.Cut the canvas order, reader — every fac: Cut the canvas order, reader. Count every face of that roof, floor included.
map.The kiosk roof is a square pyramid: base: The kiosk roof is a square pyramid: base edge 6 m, slant height 5 m. Canvas covers the base AND all four triangle sides. How much canvas in all?
map.Conceptual: the pyramid's net is one squ: Conceptual: the pyramid's net is one square plus four identical triangles. The base counts. The kiosk has a floor.
map.Opening-day eve. Fenwick's final flyer f: Opening-day eve. Fenwick's last flyer flaps on the fence: one number, no doubling.
map.He added the three faces… and stopped. E: He added the three faces… and stopped. Every one of those faces has a twin, Fenwick. Boss gate. Let's finish this.
map.Last two jobs: weatherproof the planter: Last two jobs: seal the planter crate, canvas the sandbox tent. Reader, final numbers!
Spot Fenwick's old trick too. Three locks. Brightside opens tomorrow.
map.Boss Gate: a prism, a pyramid, and the o: Boss Gate: a prism, a pyramid, and the oldest surface-area mistake there is.
map.BOSS GATE. Three locks. Wrap it all — an: BOSS GATE. Three locks. Wrap it all, and wrap it RIGHT.
map.Three locks before opening day: weatherp: Three locks before opening day: seal the planter crate (4 × 4 × 2), canvas the sandbox tent (square pyramid, base edge 4, slant 3), and beat Fenwick's 36 m² chest quote.
map.Conceptual: prism = three face pairs, do: Conceptual: prism = three face pairs, doubled. Pyramid = base + 4 triangles. And Fenwick's number is HALF of something you found at Gate 2…
map.Painted, wrapped, weatherproofed — and e: Painted, wrapped, sealed, and every square metre counted. WE BUILT THIS.
map.THE FULL STORY: VOL. 5 — BLUEPRINT FOR B: THE FULL STORY: VOL. 5 — BLUEPRINT FOR BRIGHTSIDE. The bid, the rival, and the build, from start to end.
map.Nets.A solid unfolded flat. A cube's net: Nets.A solid unfolded flat. A cube's net needs exactly six squares, and they must fold without overlapping.
map.The classic trap.Adding the three faces: The classic trap.Adding the three faces and forgetting their twins. You get exactly half the answer.
map.completed Unit 5 · Episode 3: Wrap It Up: finished Unit 5 · Episode 3: Wrap It Up and showed mastery of nets and the surface area of prisms and pyramids.
map.Unit 5 complete — the full Brightside sa: Unit 5 complete. The full Brightside story awaits in Volume 5.
map.Count: 6 ✓. Fold: the column wraps into: Count: 6 ✓. Fold: the column wraps into 4 walls, the two side squares become lid and floor. No overlaps.
map.It folds clean → it's a valid net. Count: It folds clean, so it is a valid net. Count, then fold in your head.
map.Your turn — same idea, different numbers: Your turn. Same idea, new numbers:
map.Double it: SA = 34 m². The ×2 is the twi: Double it: SA = 34 m². The ×2 is for the twins. Never skip it.
map.SA = 4 + 16 = 20 m². Square plus four tr: SA = 4 + 16 = 20 m². One square plus four triangles, every time.
map.A rival quotes the crate at 15: exactly: A rival quotes the crate at 15, exactly half of 30. The twin faces were left out.
map.The cross folds perfectly — now the coun: The cross folds perfectly. Now the count: how many faces does a cube have?
map.The cross folds clean — six squares, six: The cross folds clean: six squares, six faces, no overlaps. Chalk test passed.
map.2(18+12+6) = 72 m² — one 80 m² can cover: 2(18+12+6) = 72 m². One 80 m² can covers it, with paint left. Fenwick's 'premium' quote is already beaten.
map.That's the three faces WITHOUT their twi: That is the three faces WITHOUT their twins. The chest also has a back, a bottom, and a far end.
map.You added the edges. Surface area multip: You added the edges. For surface area, multiply each face first: length × width per face.
map.Three face pairs: 6×3, 6×2, 3×2 — sum th: Three face pairs: 6×3, 6×2, 3×2. Add them, then double.
map.36 + 4(15) = 96 m² of canvas. The roof —: 36 + 4(15) = 96 m² of canvas. The roof and the floor are covered.
map.Those are just the four triangles — the: Those are just the four triangles. The kiosk has a floor, and floors are faces.
map.You counted four BASES. There's one squa: You counted four BASES. There is one square base. Triangles come in fours.
map.Lock 3 holds. 36 is exactly HALF of the: Lock 3 holds. 36 is exactly HALF of the chest's true 72. Which mistake cuts a surface area exactly in half?
map.ALL LOCKS OPEN. 64 m² sealed, 40 m² stit: ALL LOCKS OPEN. 64 m² sealed, 40 m² stitched, and Fenwick's half-true quote is gone for good. BRIGHTSIDE OPENS TOMORROW.
